MAJOR: Dual source of truth: stage checklist derives from latest trail event while review rows show "current architect recommendation" from another store; if those diverge, the flow silently contradicts itself — define precedence and a consistency rule explicitly.

"Latest event per stage" dedupe needs a stated ordering key (monotonic sequence vs timestamp); append-only stores with equal/backwards timestamps would break the invariant silently — state and test the ordering key.

DEFERRED "must cite a follow-up backlog id" is stated as a display rule only; nothing enforces it at ingest or disposition time — a malformed DEFERRED will render a non-compliant flow instead of failing the gate.
Hardcoded section order in `show` becomes an unmaintainable contract; define a section registry/list so tests assert order from the same source rather than duplicating the order string.

Disposition key (ACTIONED/ACCEPTED/DEFERRED/REJECTED/SCOPE) is a second copy of the enum living in rendering; point it at the canonical definitions in `docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md` or the enum owner to prevent drift.

No observability for the read path: a broken section (exception mid-render) yields partial output with no marker; at minimum emit a per-section render status so HIL can tell "missing evidence" from "renderer failed".
MINOR: Recurring finding unaddressed: `_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` (or new flow-projection helpers) still risk no direct coverage for index alignment, missing item, unknown status paths; add unit tests for those private paths.
"Renders missing evidence explicitly" needs a canonical placeholder vocabulary (e.g. 'not recorded' vs 'evidence missing'); without it, partial-item tests will encode arbitrary strings that churn.
Long unpaginated terminal output is accepted as a trade-off but is the primary UX for HIL; at least cap table cell widths deterministically so diffs of rendered output are stable.
Affected docs (`REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md`) should state the flow-view contract (section order, status derivation) so future writers don't break the HIL expectations silently.
Guardrail checklist answers are not reflected in the design text (reversibility is only in rollback field; no statement of authz/tenant scope, though read-only CLI is low risk — state it explicitly).
NIT: Reuse check: confirm the checklist/status derivation logic does not re-implement what `design_guardrails`/gate checkers already compute; if duplicated, extract to the owner.
Consider a `--json`-free `--section` filter later to mitigate output size without adding an API surface; out of scope now, note it in docs.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-bounded read-only change with clean rollback and no state mutation; the language rule is satisfied (edit to shipped Python, not new logic in Python).

Top risks: divergence between event-derived status and review-derived recommendations, an unstated ordering invariant for "latest event per stage", and DEFERRED backlog-id enforcement existing only as prose.
Tests cover the stated AC paths but should directly target the projection helpers (recurring MINOR) and the ordering/dedupe invariant before Gate 1.5 approval.
